deliberate.why: Ruby names each script bundle by its wall clock, and the battery's fixture clock names each write by its own step, so the two engines' .js entries differ in count. The output card has no history (card-mod-assets set/right/asset_output.rb:9-11), so its file takes the stand-in action id Time.now.to_i (card-mod-carrierwave lib/carrier_wave/file_card_uploader.rb:147-151, 202-205, 225-226), and store_output writes it on each update (card-mod-assets set/abstract/asset_outputter.rb:36-51). The first request's Card::Assets.refresh (:cautious, card-mod-assets lib/card/assets.rb:13-27, 86-91) re-stores the 15 mod script inputs one at a time, and each re-store rewrites the bundle (card-mod-assets set/abstract/asset_inputter.rb update_referers_after_input_changed). The committed deck holds those inputs unminified (it was built under the development environment), and the refresh stores each one minified (compress_assets true, card-mod-script set/abstract/00_script.rb:18-27), so each of the 15 script writes carries different bytes and the last is the fully minified bundle; the stylesheet writes repeat identical bytes, which Ruby re-files under a new clock name every time. DECKO_STRICT_PARITY_SCRIPT_BUNDLE_CLOCK_NAMES=off (the default) names each file by its own bytes (src/card/actions/style-asset-events.ts assetOutputNameSlot), so the 15 distinct script bundles keep 15 names and the identical stylesheet bytes land on ONE name; the pin holds that default-mode file set. DECKO_STRICT_PARITY_SCRIPT_BUNDLE_CLOCK_NAMES=on restores Ruby's stand-in action id one for one (strictTs holds that run's pin); with the drive's fixture clock, one second per read, its 15 script writes keep 15 names where Ruby's wall clock lands 13 (two writes reuse a second an earlier write took and overwrite it). No fixed clock reproduces Ruby's collisions.

deliberate.why: Ruby crashes: the history mod calls revision(action, before_action) positionally and card-mod-carrierwave's override takes a keyword (ArgumentError), so restoring an old version of any File or Image card answers 500. The port restores the version, which is what the revert was written to do. The recorded 500 is what a deployed site answers (card-mod-format's server_error view); the recording no longer runs the oracle with Rails' developer error handling, so the page carries no exception message. DECKO_STRICT_PARITY_REVISION_RESTORE_500=on reproduces the crash one for one (the same 500, the same server_error page, nothing stored), and the step then passes on agreement (the pin describes the default mode).

A knock-on of restore-file-revision, not a difference of its own. The delete's configure_successful_deletion redirects to the session's *previous location (card-mod-session set/all/location_history.rb:9-17, env/location_history.rb:19-21). Ruby renders a page on the failed restore — its controller rescue shows the server_error view, whose before: :show_page fires :save_current_location — so /Parity_Cached_File joins the history at restore-file-revision and is the entry this redirect resolves to. The port does not render on that step (it restores the version, the deliberate difference pinned there), so its history still names /Parity_Pending. Every other field agrees; only the redirect target differs, and only because of the earlier step. DECKO_STRICT_PARITY_REVISION_RESTORE_500=on erases this knock-on with its cause: the strict 500 renders the server_error view through the page machinery, whose save_current_location puts /Parity Cached File into the history, and the deny's redirect then matches Ruby (the pin describes the default mode).
